validity.recommendation: No action needed on existence/classification. See separate spec/attribution entries below for value-level caveats.
validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE + CLASSIFICATION: CONFIRMED, independent of GEM, by a wide, mutually-corroborating set of live sources spanning three decades of coverage. (1) A 2020 Kazakh-government EIA working project (gov.kz, 208pp, verified via direct download + pdftotext) for a reserve loop describes the 'existing' МГ «Макат-Северный Кавказ» (main gas pipeline Makat-North Caucasus) as an 'export' line, single-strand ('однониточный, не имеет альтернативной нитки'), diameter 1420mm, and situates it in Atyrau Oblast from km 2 to at least km 361 («Макат-Северный Кавказ» (2-361 км) располагается в Атырауской области»), with defective-pipe replacement work ongoing on the 130-361 km section — i.e. an actively maintained, currently operating asset. (2) energybase.ru (Gazprom's own asset entry in this Russian industrial database; direct HTTP to our IP is geo/anti-bot-blocked ('Доступ ограничен'), but the identical live page was retrieved and independently confirmed via the r.jina.ai text-extraction mirror, which passes url_verifier) lists it as ID eb#pipe00190, type 'Pipeline', diameter 1420mm, owner PAO Gazprom. (3) The 2020/2022-2023 loop-construction news cycle (astanatimes.com, inform.kz, both live-verified) describes QazaqGaz/Intergas commissioning a 130 km, 13.147 bcm/y reserve loop 'to the EXISTING Makat-North Caucasus main pipeline' in May 2023 — that project is GEM's own P3999 (see the duplicate-check entry below), and its whole premise (a reserve loop to protect against outages on a 30+ year old single line) is only coherent if the parent P1476 pipeline is real and currently in service. (4) Gazprom's own 2005 press release (gazprom.ru, live original 000/timeout from this network but the 2013 web.archive.org snapshot is live and verified) covers a ceremony at Kizlyar, Republic of Dagestan, for a technological tie-in ('перемычка') between «Макат — Северный Кавказ» and «Моздок — Казимагомед» — a real, dated, first-party Gazprom operational event on this exact pipeline. (5) Intergas Central Asia's own 'About the Company' page lists 'Makat – Northern Caucasus MGP' and a separate 'Makat – Northern Caucasus looping' by name among the trunk systems its Atyrau Branch operates. (6) The Great Encyclopedia of Oil and Gas (ngpedia.ru) independently confirms the pipeline's commissioning and stated purpose ('введен в действие газопровод Макат - Северный Кавказ, позволивший полностью обеспечить газом закавказские ресублики'). None of these six independent, non-GEM, non-abarrelfull sources are wikidot/theodora/gem.wiki. CLASSIFICATION: PipelineType=transmission and Fuel=Gas match every source verbatim ('магистральный газопровод' = trunk/transmission gas pipeline). No misclassification found.

validity.recommendation: No merge needed. Optionally cross-reference P1476<->P3999 in RouteNotes/ResearcherNotes so the parent/loop relationship is documented on both rows, but this is not a defect.
validity.researcher_notes: DUPLICATE CHECK vs P3999 (same name 'Makat–North Caucasus Pipeline', 130.0 km, cap 13.15, Makat->Atyrau) — the orchestrator flagged this pair for adjudication. RESOLVED, NOT a duplicate/double-count: the 2020 gov.kz EIA document is literally the environmental-impact filing for the CONSTRUCTION of a 'reserve pipeline (looping) Du1020mm, 130 km long, to the EXISTING main gas pipeline Makat-North Caucasus, on the 0-130 km section' by AO Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya, with a stated design throughput of 13,146,640,080 m3/year (=13.147 bcm/y) at Du1020mm — an almost exact match to P3999's Capacity=13.15 and its 130.0 km length. Independently, astanatimes.com and inform.kz (both live-verified) describe QazaqGaz commissioning this exact 'second line'/loop in May 2023 at a construction cost of ~86 billion KZT. So P3999 is a genuine, physically distinct parallel LOOP covering only the first 130 km of P1476's 944 km corridor (built 2020-2023, decades after P1476's 1986-1988 construction), not a re-entry of the same pipe. This is analogous to other legitimate parallel-line pairs in the Kazakhstan gas roster (e.g. P2289/P5695 Bukhara-Ural). No merge recommended; P1476 (the original 944 km trunk) and P3999 (the 130 km loop) should both stand.

validity.recommendation: Keep Diameter='1200, 1400, 1420' mm as-is; add the three refs below. No change needed.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — Diameter, WELL CORROBORATED, tier=high. GEM's multi-value '1200, 1400, 1420' mm is explained precisely by an independent Ukrainian pipeline-construction contractor's project table (vtg.com.ua, live page now 404 but the 2022-02-25 web.archive.org snapshot — contemporaneous with when gem.wiki cites it — is live and verified), which lists 'Макат-Сев.Кавказ' with two diameter/pressure/length triples: 1400mm @ 7.4 MPa for 896 km, and 1200mm @ 5.4 MPa for 48 km, each a single strand ('1' 'K-во ниток'), through Kazakhstan and Russia — 896+48 = 944 km EXACTLY matching GEM's LengthKnown. The 1400mm figure is not a conflict with the 1420mm figure: it is the SAME pipe under two standard Russian/Soviet pipeline-industry conventions — 'Du' (nominal bore, условный диаметр) vs. actual outer diameter, which for this pipe class differ by the standard 20mm (Du1400 = 1420mm OD) — and this exact 1420mm OD figure for the main run is independently confirmed TWICE more: by the 2020 gov.kz EIA document ('диаметр газопровода – 1420 мм') and by energybase.ru ('Диаметр труб 1420 мм'). So all three GEM diameter values are accounted for by three mutually independent sources: the 896 km/1400-1420mm main run (vtg.com.ua + gov.kz + energybase, all agreeing once the Du/OD convention is understood) plus a genuine, distinct 48 km/1200mm section (vtg.com.ua only). No fabrication, no misclassification.

validity.recommendation: Do NOT change LengthKnown (944.00) or Capacity (21.90) — both are well-supported by sources independent of energybase.ru. But log the conflict in ResearcherNotes rather than silently passing it: energybase.ru states 492 km / 42 bcm/y for the same named pipeline, roughly half/double GEM's figures. Recommend Update spot-check whether energybase's page scopes to only the Kazakhstan-territory segment (its 492 km almost exactly matches an incomplete/fragmentary OSM trace of ~495 km, suggesting a shared partial-geometry origin for both numbers rather than a true competing full-route measurement) before treating it as an independent competing claim.
validity.researcher_notes: SPEC — Length + Capacity, MATERIAL DISAGREEMENT FOUND, flagged per standing rule 4/5 rather than silently passed. Two independent sources corroborate GEM's CURRENT values closely: (1) vtg.com.ua's project table sums to 896+48=944 km EXACTLY (see the diameter entry above for detail) — an unusually precise match, since it is not a rounded total but the sum of two distinct, differently-specified pipe sections. (2) cdu.ru (центральное диспетчерское управление топливно-энергетического комплекса России, the Russian state fuel/energy dispatch directorate — a genuinely independent, official origin, distinct from GEM, energybase and vtg.com.ua) states verbatim: '«Макат — Северный Кавказ» (среднеазиатский газ; пропускная способность — 21,9 млрд куб. м в год)' — an EXACT match to GEM's Capacity=21.90. HOWEVER, energybase.ru (accessed via r.jina.ai mirror since it geo/anti-bot-blocks direct fetches) states, for the SAME named pipeline: 'Protyazhennost 492 km' / 'Moshchnost 42 mlrd. m3/god' — almost exactly HALF the length and DOUBLE the capacity of GEM's values. This is not a trivial rounding difference (standing rule 4's >materially threshold is clearly met on both fields). Two observations bear on how to weigh it: (a) energybase's diameter (1420mm) and construction/start years (1986/1988) on the SAME page are an EXACT match to GEM and to the other independent sources — so energybase is not simply an unreliable/garbage source, just internally inconsistent on length/capacity specifically; (b) energybase's 492 km is suspiciously close to an OSM-mapped trace for this same named relation (8203643, 8 member ways) that likewise sums to only ~495 km of DRAWN geometry, despite that relation's own node bounding box spanning from Makat (47.68N, 53.34E) to a point 43.58N/45.90E (~30 km from Grozny) — a straight-line span of ~737 km, meaning the true route must be materially LONGER than 495 km even in the straight-line case, so the OSM trace is geometrically fragmentary/incomplete, not a complete shorter alternate route. The coincidence between energybase's 492 km and OSM's ~495 km (both landing well short of the geometrically-required minimum) is the strongest lead I found for WHY energybase disagrees — both may trace to the same incomplete mapped/GIS extent rather than a true full-route re-measurement — but I could not prove this and am not overwriting GEM's value on that inference alone. Net: keeping GEM's 944 km / 21.90 bcm/y (each backed by one clean independent source, vtg.com.ua and cdu.ru respectively) over energybase's conflicting 492/42, but this is flagged, not silently resolved, per the standing rule.

validity.recommendation: Consider adding QazaqGaz / Intergas Central Asia (or 'National Company QazaqGaz JSC') as a second Owner entry with a percent split, rather than Owner1=Gazprom PJSC 100%. I could not find a source stating an explicit ownership percentage for either party on this specific line, so I'm not proposing a specific split — flagging for Update to dig into a KZ-RF intergovernmental gas-transit agreement or QazaqGaz's own asset register if one is findable.
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION — Owner. GEM's current value is Owner1=Gazprom PJSC, 100%. I could not find any source that explicitly states an OWNERSHIP percentage split for this specific pipeline, so I cannot confirm or refute the 100%-Gazprom figure directly. But I found clear, repeated, first-party evidence that the KAZAKHSTAN-territory segment is at minimum OPERATED/maintained by AO Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya (a subsidiary of National Company QazaqGaz JSC), not by Gazprom directly: (1) intergas.kz's own 'About the Company' page lists 'Makat – Northern Caucasus MGP' and 'Makat – Northern Caucasus looping' by name under its Atyrau Branch, among pipelines it 'operates' as the government-designated 'National Operator on the Main Gas Pipelines Transmission' (status granted July 2018); the same page notes the company's total operated network includes '7,173 km of the third party's networks contracted to the Company for technical maintenance' — i.e. Intergas explicitly distinguishes networks it OWNS from third-party-owned networks it merely maintains, so this listing alone does not resolve which bucket Makat-North Caucasus falls in. (2) the 2020 gov.kz EIA document names AO 'Intergaz Tsentralnaya Aziya' as the CUSTOMER/заказчик commissioning capital work on this exact pipeline. Given the pipeline is Soviet-era (built 1986-1988) cross-border infrastructure, it is plausible GEM's Gazprom-100% figure reflects a legacy ownership arrangement that survived the USSR's dissolution (as is true for some other Central-Asia-Center-family lines), with Intergas providing contracted O&M on the Kazakh section without owning it — which would make GEM's value correct, just incompletely explained by a citable source. I am not calling this a confirmed error, but it is a real attribution gap worth a closer look, not a rubber stamp.

validity.recommendation: No change proposed to EndState/Province=Chechnya (geometry supports it), but flag for Update/RouteNotes that the pipeline's Russian-side infrastructure is genuinely multi-region (Kalmykia/Dagestan tie-ins exist along the corridor), so 'Chechnya' alone should not be read as excluding transit through other Russian regions.
validity.researcher_notes: ATTRIBUTION — EndState/Province='Chechnya'. I could not find a source that says the word 'Grozny' or 'Chechnya' explicitly for this pipeline's terminus — every live source I reached describes the destination only generically as 'North Caucasus' / 'Transcaucasian republics' (ngpedia.ru) or names OTHER Russian regions along the corridor: a 2005 Gazprom press release (gazprom.ru, verified via web.archive.org) describes a ceremony at Kizlyar, REPUBLIC OF DAGESTAN, commissioning a tie-in between this pipeline and «Моздок — Казимагомед», and general search results independently describe 130 km of this pipeline's route running through Dagestan territory, plus an unverified secondary mention of a compressor station ('Артезиан') in the Chernozemelsky district of the Republic of KALMYKIA. However, I pulled the OSM relation (8203643, 'Makat–North Caucasus', 8 ways) directly and its member-node bounding box runs from Makat (47.68N/53.34E) down to 43.58N/45.90E — which is only ~30 km from GROZNY — so the mapped geometry itself DOES support a Chechnya-area terminus, consistent with GEM's current value and with the pipeline's likely original Soviet-era design purpose (Grozny was a major Caucasus oil/gas hub). My best read: the pipeline's Russian routing genuinely passes through MULTIPLE regions on its way from the Kazakh border to the North Caucasus (plausibly Kalmykia, then Dagestan via the Kizlyar tie-in, continuing toward Chechnya), and the 2005 Dagestan tie-in is most likely a supplementary interconnection to the separate Mozdok-Kazimagomed system rather than a redefinition of THIS pipeline's own endpoint. I am not recommending a value change since the geometry backs 'Chechnya', but the single-province attribution is not textually nailed down by any source I could independently verify, and the route is clearly more multi-region than a single EndState/Province field can capture.

fills.researcher_notes: Status inferred by context, not a literal word match (per url_verifier docstring on STATUS): the 2020 EIA document describes active defective-pipe replacement/repair work on an in-service line, and cdu.ru's 2023 TEK report lists it among Kazakhstan's currently operating trunk export pipelines with a stated throughput. See the dedicated diameter validity entry above: vtg.com.ua gives 1400mm/896km + 1200mm/48km directly; gov.kz's EIA doc and energybase.ru both independently give 1420mm (the OD-vs-Du naming equivalent of 1400mm) for the main run. All three GEM values are accounted for.

Makat is confirmed as the pipeline's own origin point/name by every source (the pipeline is literally named for it); this is a definitional match, not a separate discovered fact, but both refs name Makat as the KS/starting point.

StartLocation=Makat/StartState-Province=Atyrau/StartCountryOrArea=Kazakhstan are well confirmed (gov.kz doc's Makatskoye/Redutskoye LPU are in Atyrau Oblast; vtg.com.ua lists Kazakhstan as a transited country). EndCountryOrArea=Russia is confirmed (both sources list Russia). EndState/Province=Chechnya is the weaker link in this cluster — see the dedicated attribution-caveat validity entry above: no source names Grozny/Chechnya explicitly, but OSM geometry for the named relation terminates ~30 km from Grozny, and the route is more genuinely multi-region (Kalmykia/Dagestan infrastructure also documented along the corridor) than a single end-province can capture. Tier kept at medium rather than high because of that specific field's weaker sourcing.

Could not independently confirm a 100%-Gazprom ownership split. What I DID confirm: intergas.kz's 'About the Company' page names this pipeline among assets its Atyrau Branch operates as Kazakhstan's designated National Operator, while separately noting some of its operated network is third-party-owned and only contracted to it for maintenance — which is consistent with, but does not itself state, Gazprom ownership. See the dedicated attribution-caveat validity entry above. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than citing a source that doesn't actually state the ownership percentage.

summary: P1476 (Makat–North Caucasus, 944 km, 21.9 bcm/y): existence and classification CONFIRMED by 6 independent non-GEM sources; P3999 (130 km loop) confirmed as a genuine parallel reserve line, not a duplicate; diameter (1200/1400/1420mm) fully corroborated once the Du-vs-OD naming convention is understood. FLAGGED (spec concern, not resolved): energybase.ru gives a materially conflicting 492 km / 42 bcm/y for the same pipeline — kept GEM's values (each independently backed by vtg.com.ua/cdu.ru) but logged the conflict per standing rule. FLAGGED (attribution caveats): Owner=Gazprom-100% is plausible but unconfirmed by any source with an actual percentage (UNRESOLVED, not fabricated); EndState/Province=Chechnya is geometrically supported by OSM but not textually confirmed by name, and the route is more multi-region (Kalmykia/Dagestan infrastructure also documented) than one field captures.
